title: Nika riots break out in Constantinople
summary: Chariot racing factions at the Hippodrome turned on Emperor Justinian I and set much of Constantinople on fire. After several days the revolt was crushed with the massacre of tens of thousands of people in the Hippodrome.
reason: Anger over heavy taxes, harsh officials and the arrest of faction members united the normally rival Blues and Greens against the emperor.
significance: Justinian survived and used the destruction to rebuild the city, including the new Hagia Sophia.

title: Hagia Sophia is consecrated
summary: Emperor Justinian I dedicated the new church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, built in under six years. Its vast dome made it the largest church in the world for nearly a thousand years.
reason: The earlier church had burned in the Nika riots, and Justinian wanted a monument to his rule and to Christian faith.
significance: It became a model for Byzantine and later Ottoman architecture and a symbol of the city.

title: Pakal the Great becomes ruler of Palenque
summary: K'inich Janaab' Pakal took the throne of the Maya city of Palenque at the age of twelve. He ruled for 68 years and oversaw the building of its finest temples and palaces.
reason: Palenque had suffered defeats by Calakmul, and the young heir was installed to restore the dynasty.
significance: His reign made Palenque one of the great Maya cities, and his tomb is among the richest finds of Maya archaeology.

title: Li Yuan proclaims the Tang dynasty
summary: Li Yuan declared himself emperor in Chang'an, founding the Tang dynasty as the Sui dynasty collapsed. He is known as Emperor Gaozu of Tang.
reason: Failed wars in Korea, costly public works and revolts had broken Sui rule, and the murder of Emperor Yang left the throne open.
significance: The Tang ruled China for almost three centuries in a golden age of culture, trade and power.

title: Muslims defeat the Quraysh at the Battle of Badr
summary: A small force led by Muhammad defeated a larger army of the Quraysh of Mecca near the wells of Badr. Several leading Meccans were killed.
reason: The Muslims of Medina had moved to intercept a Meccan caravan, and Mecca sent an army to protect it.
significance: The victory strengthened Muhammad's position in Arabia and is remembered in Islam as a sign of divine support.

title: Li Shimin seizes power in the Xuanwu Gate Incident
summary: Prince Li Shimin ambushed and killed his brothers, the crown prince Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji, at the Xuanwu Gate of the palace in Chang'an. Within weeks his father abdicated in his favor.
reason: A bitter rivalry over the succession had grown between Li Shimin, the dynasty's leading general, and the crown prince.
significance: Li Shimin became Emperor Taizong, one of the most admired rulers in Chinese history.

title: Death of the Prophet Muhammad
summary: Muhammad died in Medina after a short illness, having united much of Arabia under Islam. Abu Bakr was chosen as the first caliph.
reason: He fell ill with a fever shortly after his farewell pilgrimage to Mecca.
significance: The question of his succession shaped the caliphate and the later split between Sunni and Shia Islam.

title: Battle of the Yarmouk begins
summary: The armies of the Rashidun Caliphate under Khalid ibn al-Walid met a large Byzantine army by the Yarmouk River. After six days of fighting the Byzantines were routed.
reason: Emperor Heraclius gathered a great army to drive back the Arab conquest of Syria.
significance: The defeat ended Byzantine rule in Syria and opened the Levant to the spread of Islam.
place: Yarmouk River, near the Syria-Jordan border

title: Caliph Uthman is assassinated in Medina
summary: Rebels besieged the house of the third caliph, Uthman ibn Affan, and killed him while he was reading the Quran. Ali ibn Abi Talib then became caliph.
reason: Many provincial Muslims resented Uthman's favoring of his own Umayyad clan and his choice of governors.
significance: His death led to the First Fitna, the first civil war within the Muslim community.

title: Husayn ibn Ali is killed at the Battle of Karbala
summary: A small group led by Husayn ibn Ali, grandson of Muhammad, was surrounded and killed by an Umayyad army at Karbala. The women and children of his family were taken captive.
reason: Husayn refused to accept Yazid I as caliph and was travelling to Kufa, where supporters had invited him to lead them.
significance: His death is mourned every year on Ashura and became central to Shia Islam.

title: Wu Zetian becomes China's only empress regnant
summary: Wu Zetian, who had long ruled through her husband and sons, took the throne in her own name and proclaimed a new Zhou dynasty. She ruled until 705.
reason: After decades of controlling the Tang court, she removed her son Emperor Ruizong and claimed full imperial authority.
significance: She remains the only woman in Chinese history to rule as emperor in her own right.

title: Charles Martel defeats the Umayyads at the Battle of Tours
summary: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeated an Umayyad army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi between Poitiers and Tours. The Umayyad commander was killed.
reason: After conquering Iberia, Umayyad armies were raiding north into Gaul, and this force was heading for the rich abbey of Tours.
significance: It halted the northward advance of the caliphate into Western Europe and raised the power of the Carolingian family.

title: Death of the Venerable Bede
summary: The monk and scholar Bede died at the monastery of Jarrow in Northumbria. He had completed the Ecclesiastical History of the English People a few years before.
reason: He died of old age after a life of study and writing in the monastery he entered as a child.
significance: His history is the main source for early England, and he made dating years from the birth of Christ widely used.

title: The Abbasids defeat the Umayyads at the Battle of the Zab
summary: An Abbasid army crushed the forces of the Umayyad caliph Marwan II by the Great Zab River. Marwan fled and was killed later that year.
reason: The Abbasid revolution, launched in Khurasan, drew on wide discontent with Umayyad rule among non-Arab Muslims and Shia supporters.
significance: It ended the Umayyad Caliphate in the east and brought the Abbasids to power for five centuries.

title: An Lushan launches his rebellion against the Tang
summary: The frontier general An Lushan marched south from his base at Fanyang against the Tang court. He soon took Luoyang and Chang'an and proclaimed his own dynasty.
reason: An Lushan commanded huge armies in the northeast and feared the hostility of the chief minister Yang Guozhong.
significance: The eight-year war killed millions and permanently weakened the Tang dynasty.

title: Caliph al-Mansur founds Baghdad
summary: The Abbasid caliph al-Mansur laid the foundations of a new capital, the round city of Baghdad, on the Tigris. It was planned as a circle with the palace and mosque at its centre.
reason: The Abbasids wanted a capital away from Umayyad Syria, near their supporters in Iraq and Persia and on major trade routes.
significance: Baghdad became the largest city of its age and the centre of the Islamic Golden Age.

title: Charlemagne is crowned emperor in Rome
summary: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne as emperor of the Romans in St. Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day.
reason: Charlemagne had protected the pope from his enemies in Rome and ruled most of Western Europe, while the throne in Constantinople was held by a woman, Irene.
significance: It revived the idea of a Western empire and led to the Holy Roman Empire.
place: Old St. Peter's Basilica, Rome, Vatican City

title: Death of Caliph Harun al-Rashid
summary: The Abbasid caliph Harun al-Rashid died at Tus in Khurasan while on campaign against a rebellion. His empire was divided between his sons al-Amin and al-Ma'mun.
reason: He fell ill while marching east to put down a revolt in Khurasan.
significance: His reign was remembered as the height of Abbasid Baghdad, and the split between his sons led to civil war.

title: Oaths of Strasbourg are sworn
summary: Louis the German and Charles the Bald swore an alliance against their brother Lothair, each in the language of the other's army. The texts were recorded in early forms of French and German.
reason: Charlemagne's grandsons were fighting over the division of the Carolingian Empire.
significance: The oaths are the oldest surviving text in a Romance language that became French.

title: The Diamond Sutra, oldest dated printed book, is made
summary: A woodblock printed copy of the Buddhist Diamond Sutra was produced in Tang China, with a note giving this date. It was found in the Mogao Caves at Dunhuang in 1900.
reason: A man named Wang Jie paid for the printing for the merit of his parents, as Buddhists spread scripture through copies.
significance: It is the earliest dated printed book known, evidence of the Chinese invention of printing.

title: Jogan earthquake and tsunami strike northeast Japan
summary: A great earthquake off the Sanriku coast sent a tsunami over the Sendai plain, flooding the area around the fortress of Taga and drowning about a thousand people.
reason: It was caused by a rupture on the subduction zone off northeastern Honshu.
significance: Its records warned of the kind of tsunami that struck the same coast in 2011.

title: Death of Alfred the Great
summary: Alfred, king of Wessex, died in Winchester after a reign spent defending his kingdom against the Vikings. He was succeeded by his son Edward the Elder.
reason: He died after years of ill health.
significance: His defence of Wessex and support for learning laid the ground for a united kingdom of England.

title: Abd al-Rahman III proclaims the Caliphate of Cordoba
summary: The Umayyad emir of al-Andalus, Abd al-Rahman III, declared himself caliph in Cordoba, rejecting the authority of both the Abbasids and the Fatimids.
reason: He had restored order in al-Andalus and wanted to answer the Fatimids, who had claimed the caliphate in North Africa.
significance: Cordoba became one of the richest and most learned cities of Europe.

title: Otto I defeats the Magyars at the Battle of Lechfeld
summary: King Otto I of Germany destroyed a large Hungarian army that was besieging Augsburg, on the plain by the river Lech.
reason: Magyar horsemen had raided Western Europe for decades and invaded Bavaria again in 955.
significance: It ended the Hungarian raids, and the Magyars settled and soon became a Christian kingdom.

title: Zhao Kuangyin founds the Song dynasty
summary: After his troops proclaimed him emperor at Chen Bridge, the general Zhao Kuangyin took the throne from the child ruler of the Later Zhou and founded the Song dynasty.
reason: Northern China had suffered a series of short military regimes, and the army wanted a strong adult ruler.
significance: The Song reunified most of China and presided over a great age of commerce, technology and learning.

title: Otto I is crowned Holy Roman Emperor
summary: Pope John XII crowned the German king Otto I as emperor in Rome.
reason: The pope needed protection against Berengar II of Italy, and Otto wanted the imperial title after his victories.
significance: It began the line of German emperors usually counted as the Holy Roman Empire.
place: Old St. Peter's Basilica, Rome, Vatican City

title: Hugh Capet is crowned king of the Franks
summary: Hugh Capet was crowned king of West Francia after the death of the last Carolingian king, Louis V.
reason: The great nobles and the archbishop of Reims chose Hugh over the Carolingian claimant Charles of Lorraine.
significance: His Capetian dynasty and its branches ruled France until the Revolution.

title: Astronomers record the supernova that made the Crab Nebula
summary: Chinese astronomers of the Song court recorded a guest star bright enough to be seen in daylight for weeks. It was the explosion that left the Crab Nebula.
reason: A massive star in the constellation Taurus ended its life in a supernova.
significance: Its records let modern astronomers date the Crab Nebula and its pulsar exactly.

title: Papal legates excommunicate the Patriarch of Constantinople
summary: Cardinal Humbert placed a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar of Hagia Sophia, and the patriarch answered by excommunicating the legates.
reason: Rome and Constantinople had long disagreed over papal authority, the Creed and church customs.
significance: It is the traditional date of the split between the Catholic and Orthodox churches.

title: Westminster Abbey is consecrated
summary: The great Romanesque church built by Edward the Confessor at Westminster was consecrated. The king was too ill to attend and died days later.
reason: Edward had rebuilt the abbey as a royal church and his intended burial place.
significance: It became the coronation church of English and British monarchs.

title: William of Normandy wins the Battle of Hastings
summary: The Norman army of Duke William defeated the English under King Harold Godwinson, who was killed in the battle.
reason: William claimed the English throne after the death of Edward the Confessor and invaded when Harold was crowned.
significance: The Norman Conquest transformed England's rulers, language, law and ties to Europe.

title: Seljuks defeat the Byzantines at Manzikert
summary: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeated a Byzantine army and captured Emperor Romanos IV Diogenes near Manzikert in eastern Anatolia.
reason: Romanos marched east to stop Turkish raids into Byzantine Armenia and Anatolia.
significance: It opened Anatolia to Turkish settlement and led Byzantium to ask the West for help, a cause of the Crusades.

title: Pope Urban II calls for the First Crusade
summary: At the Council of Clermont, Pope Urban II urged Western Christians to march east to help Byzantium and free Jerusalem. The crowd answered with the cry Deus vult.
reason: Byzantine Emperor Alexios I had asked for soldiers against the Seljuks, and the pope also sought to assert papal leadership.
significance: It launched two centuries of crusading wars between Latin Christians and the Muslim world.

title: Crusaders capture Jerusalem
summary: Armies of the First Crusade broke into Jerusalem after a five-week siege and massacred much of its Muslim and Jewish population.
reason: Freeing the holy city was the goal of the crusade, and Fatimid Egypt had only recently retaken it from the Seljuks.
significance: It founded the Kingdom of Jerusalem and left a long memory of crusader violence in the region.

title: The Concordat of Worms ends the Investiture Controversy
summary: Emperor Henry V and Pope Callixtus II agreed that the Church would choose and invest bishops with their spiritual authority, while the emperor kept a role in granting their lands.
reason: For half a century popes and emperors had fought over who had the right to appoint bishops.
significance: It set an early boundary between church and state power in Europe.

title: Earthquake devastates Aleppo and northern Syria
summary: A powerful earthquake struck Aleppo and the surrounding region, destroying towns and fortresses and killing a great many people.
reason: It was caused by movement on the Dead Sea Transform fault system.
significance: It is counted among the deadliest earthquakes in recorded history.

title: Treaty of Zamora recognizes the Kingdom of Portugal
summary: Alfonso VII of Leon accepted Afonso Henriques as king of Portugal in a meeting at Zamora.
reason: Afonso Henriques had won battles against the Moors and against Leon and had already been calling himself king.
significance: It is taken as the founding date of Portugal as an independent kingdom.
participants: Alfonso VII of Leon and Castile

title: Abbot Suger consecrates the new choir of Saint-Denis
summary: The rebuilt choir of the abbey church of Saint-Denis, with pointed arches, ribbed vaults and large stained glass windows, was consecrated in the presence of King Louis VII.
reason: Abbot Suger wanted a church filled with light to honor God and the French monarchy, whose kings were buried there.
significance: It is considered the first Gothic building, the start of a style that spread across Europe.

title: Archbishop Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury
summary: Four knights of King Henry II killed Thomas Becket, Archbishop of Canterbury, inside his cathedral.
reason: Becket had resisted the king's attempts to control the Church, and the knights acted on Henry's angry words.
significance: Becket was quickly made a saint, and Henry had to do public penance and give way on church rights.

title: The Minamoto destroy the Taira at Dan-no-ura
summary: In a naval battle in the Shimonoseki Strait, the Minamoto fleet defeated the Taira clan. The child emperor Antoku drowned with many of the Taira.
reason: It was the final battle of the Genpei War between the two great warrior clans for control of Japan.
significance: Minamoto no Yoritomo went on to found the Kamakura shogunate and centuries of warrior rule.

title: Saladin crushes the crusaders at the Battle of Hattin
summary: Saladin's army surrounded and destroyed the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem near the Horns of Hattin. King Guy of Lusignan was captured.
reason: Saladin had united Egypt and Syria and declared war after crusader attacks on Muslim caravans.
significance: The defeat left the crusader states almost defenceless and led to the fall of Jerusalem.
place: Horns of Hattin, near Tiberias, Israel

title: Saladin captures Jerusalem
summary: After a short siege, the defenders of Jerusalem under Balian of Ibelin surrendered the city to Saladin, who allowed most inhabitants to leave on payment of a ransom.
reason: The crusader army had been destroyed at Hattin, leaving the city with few soldiers.
significance: Its loss shocked Europe and provoked the Third Crusade.

title: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa drowns on crusade
summary: Holy Roman Emperor Frederick I Barbarossa drowned while crossing the Saleph River in Cilicia on his way to the Holy Land.
reason: He was leading a large German army in the Third Crusade to retake Jerusalem.
significance: Without him most of the German army broke up, weakening the crusade.

title: Death of Saladin in Damascus
summary: Saladin, sultan of Egypt and Syria and conqueror of Jerusalem, died of a fever in Damascus.
reason: He fell ill a few months after making peace with Richard the Lionheart.
significance: He was admired by Muslims and Christians alike, and his empire was divided among his heirs.

title: Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople
summary: Crusaders and Venetians stormed Constantinople and plundered the city for three days, then set up a Latin Empire in its place.
reason: The crusaders were deep in debt to Venice and had been drawn into a Byzantine succession dispute that broke down into war.
significance: It shattered the Byzantine Empire and deepened the hostility between Catholic and Orthodox Christians.

title: Christian kingdoms defeat the Almohads at Las Navas de Tolosa
summary: The united armies of Castile, Aragon, Navarre and Portugal defeated the Almohad caliph Muhammad al-Nasir in the Sierra Morena.
reason: After the Christian defeat at Alarcos, Pope Innocent III backed a crusade and the Iberian kings joined forces.
significance: It broke Almohad power and opened southern Spain to the Christian reconquest.
wikipedia: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa

title: Philip II of France wins the Battle of Bouvines
summary: King Philip II Augustus defeated the allied army of Emperor Otto IV, the Count of Flanders and English forces of King John near Bouvines.
reason: King John and his allies hoped to crush France and recover the English lands Philip had taken.
significance: It made France a leading power and helped force King John to accept Magna Carta.

title: King John agrees to Magna Carta at Runnymede
summary: Faced with rebel barons, King John of England set his seal to a charter of liberties at Runnymede beside the Thames.
reason: Heavy taxes, arbitrary rule and military failure in France had driven the barons to revolt.
significance: It became a lasting symbol of the principle that rulers are bound by law.

title: Fourth Lateran Council opens in Rome
summary: Pope Innocent III opened a great council of bishops in the Lateran Palace, which defined transubstantiation, required yearly confession and set rules for Jews and heretics.
reason: Innocent wanted to reform the Church, fight heresy and prepare a new crusade.
significance: Its decrees shaped Catholic practice for centuries.

title: Pope Honorius III approves the Dominican Order
summary: Pope Honorius III issued a bull confirming the Order of Preachers founded by Dominic de Guzman.
reason: Dominic wanted educated, poor preachers to counter heresy in southern France.
significance: The Dominicans became one of the most influential orders in teaching, theology and later the Inquisition.

title: Mongols defeat the Rus at the Kalka River
summary: A Mongol force under Jebe and Subutai routed a combined army of Rus princes and Cumans by the Kalka River.
reason: The Cumans asked the Rus for help against the Mongols, who were returning from a great raid around the Caspian.
significance: It was the first clash between the Mongols and the Rus, a warning of the conquest that followed.

title: Death of Francis of Assisi
summary: Francis of Assisi, founder of the Franciscan friars, died at the Porziuncola chapel near Assisi. He was made a saint less than two years later.
reason: His health had been broken by illness and his life of poverty.
significance: His order and his ideal of poverty and love of nature deeply shaped Christianity.

title: Mongols capture and destroy Kiev
summary: The Mongol army of Batu Khan stormed Kiev after a siege, killing most of its people and burning the city.
reason: The Mongols were conquering the Rus principalities as part of their great western campaign.
significance: It ended Kiev's role as the centre of the Rus, which came under the Golden Horde.

title: Mongols destroy the Hungarian army at Mohi
summary: The Mongols under Batu and Subutai crushed the army of King Bela IV of Hungary by the Sajo River. Much of Hungary was then ravaged.
reason: Hungary had sheltered the Cumans fleeing the Mongols and stood in the path of their invasion of Europe.
significance: It was the Mongols' greatest victory in Europe and devastated the kingdom of Hungary.
place: Muhi, near the Sajo River, Hungary

title: Death of the Great Khan Ogedei
summary: Ogedei, son of Genghis Khan and Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, died after a night of heavy drinking.
reason: He had long suffered from alcoholism.
significance: The news led the Mongol princes in Europe to turn back to settle the succession, sparing Western Europe.

title: Mongols capture Baghdad and end the Abbasid Caliphate
summary: Hulegu's Mongol army took Baghdad after a short siege. The city was sacked, the caliph al-Musta'sim was executed and a vast number of people were killed.
reason: The caliph had refused to submit to Hulegu, who was extending Mongol rule over the Middle East.
significance: It ended the Abbasid Caliphate in Baghdad and is often seen as the end of the Islamic Golden Age.

title: Mamluks defeat the Mongols at Ain Jalut
summary: The Mamluk army of Egypt under Qutuz and Baybars defeated a Mongol force in the Jezreel Valley of Palestine.
reason: After taking Baghdad and Syria the Mongols threatened Egypt, but most of their army had withdrawn after the death of the Great Khan.
significance: It stopped the Mongol advance into the Middle East and Africa and made the Mamluks the leading Muslim power.

title: Nicaean forces retake Constantinople
summary: A small Nicaean force under Alexios Strategopoulos entered Constantinople while its Latin garrison was away, ending the Latin Empire.
reason: The Empire of Nicaea had been rebuilding Byzantine power in Anatolia and Greece since the sack of 1204.
significance: Michael VIII Palaiologos restored the Byzantine Empire, which lasted until 1453.

title: Simon de Montfort's Parliament meets
summary: Simon de Montfort, who held power after defeating Henry III, called a parliament in Westminster that included elected knights from the shires and burgesses from the towns.
reason: Montfort needed wide support for his government against the royalists.
significance: It is seen as a forerunner of the House of Commons and of representative government.

title: Kublai Khan proclaims the Yuan dynasty
summary: Kublai Khan adopted the Chinese dynastic name Great Yuan for his realm, ruling as a Chinese emperor from his new capital Dadu.
reason: Kublai wanted to present Mongol rule as a legitimate Chinese dynasty as he prepared to finish the conquest of the Song.
significance: The Yuan was the first foreign dynasty to rule all of China.

title: Death of Thomas Aquinas
summary: The Dominican theologian Thomas Aquinas died at the abbey of Fossanova while travelling to the Second Council of Lyon. His Summa Theologica was left unfinished.
reason: He fell ill on the journey, possibly after a head injury.
significance: His joining of Aristotle's philosophy with Christian theology became the basis of Catholic thought.

title: Yuan fleet destroys the last Song forces at Yamen
summary: The Yuan navy defeated the last fleet of the Southern Song off Yamen. The minister Lu Xiufu jumped into the sea with the boy emperor Zhao Bing.
reason: The Song court had fled south after the fall of its capital Lin'an, and Kublai's forces pursued it to the coast.
significance: It ended the Song dynasty and completed the Mongol conquest of China.

title: The Sicilian Vespers revolt against French rule
summary: At the hour of vespers on Easter Monday, the people of Palermo rose against the French soldiers of Charles of Anjou, and the revolt spread across Sicily.
reason: Sicilians resented heavy taxes and the harsh rule of the Angevin French.
significance: Sicily passed to the Crown of Aragon, starting a long war over southern Italy.

title: St. Lucia's flood drowns thousands in the Low Countries
summary: A storm surge on the North Sea broke through dunes and dikes in the Netherlands and northern Germany, killing tens of thousands of people.
reason: A powerful storm drove the sea over low lying land already weakened by earlier floods.
significance: It is one of the deadliest floods in history and greatly widened the Zuiderzee.

title: Tran Hung Dao defeats the Yuan fleet at Bach Dang
summary: Vietnamese forces led by Tran Hung Dao trapped the Yuan fleet on iron-tipped stakes driven into the bed of the Bach Dang River at low tide and destroyed it.
reason: Kublai Khan had sent a third invasion to conquer Dai Viet after earlier failures.
significance: It ended Mongol attempts to conquer Vietnam and made Tran Hung Dao a national hero.
place: Bach Dang River, Quang Ninh, Vietnam

title: Mamluks capture Acre, the last crusader stronghold
summary: The Mamluk army of Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil stormed Acre after a six-week siege. The remaining crusader towns on the coast were abandoned soon after.
reason: The Mamluks were driving the last Latin Christians from the Levant, and a massacre of Muslims in Acre gave them a pretext.
significance: It ended the crusader states in the Holy Land.
